outcome: persistent depressive symptoms (positive EPDS screen postpartum)
cohort: The study included 3240 pregnancies where an Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) screening was completed at both obstetrics (prenatal) and pediatrics (postpartum) within an integrated healthcare system.
finding: Black women were more likely to screen positive for depression prenatally, and over one-third of women experienced persistent positive depression screens from pregnancy into the postpartum period, with higher prenatal EPDS scores predicting persistence.
